# Recorded-frame fixtures

Each fixture is a pair of files with the same stem:

* `<name>.log` — CAN frames in `candump -l` format
  (`(epoch.micro) iface ID#HEX`), recorded from a real MTS160 through the
  driver's `~/raw` topic.
* `<name>.json` — one segment per settled reading with the fixture position
  (`printer`: x/y/z/e/yaw), the physical truth (`truth`), and `expect`.

The `expect` blocks are **regression labels**: they were computed from the
frames inside each segment (mean left position / angle with a ±1.5
tolerance, minimum strength, `tape_detected` when the strength never dropped
to 0). They pin down what the decoder and the driver must reproduce.

| fixture | what was recorded (sensor at yaw 0, 20 mm height) |
|---|---|
| `idle_no_tape` | sensor away from any tape: strength 0, positions 0 |
| `lateral` | a tape crossed laterally in 1 mm steps: the position ramps −58…+43 mm |
| `lateral_h15`, `lateral_h40` | the same crossing at 15 mm and 40 mm height (the tape is lost early at 40 mm) |
| `fork_yaw+0` / `merge_yaw+0` | a tape followed through a branch point and back (fork / merge flags) |
| `marker_alongside_yaw0` | a 20 mm point marker beside the tape (TPDO2 marker X/Y, left-marker flag) |
| `navicode_off+0_step2_forward` / `_back` | a navicode section in 2 mm stop-and-go steps; no code was decoded (counter unchanged), so these pin the *no-change* behaviour of `is_new` |

`test_replay.py` runs every pair through the decoder and through the live
driver node (python-can `virtual` in-process, the node in its own namespace so
a driver running on the host cannot interfere; `vcan0` via socketcan when the
interface exists). `synthetic_*.log` files are generated by the tests
themselves and must not be committed.
